title: Onboard ramp: access readiness and latency review
summary: Weekly POC checkpoint focused on staging access, VPC peering, KMS handoff, and preliminary latency/throughput findings. Agreed follow-ups: grant remaining staging ports, run 10k token LAT test with quantized model, and provide SOC2 excerpt. Identified two blockers: egress rules for telemetry pipeline and customer KMS cert rotation policy.
next_steps: Redwood to open support ticket for peering error logs and share request ID (Maya)
Customer to approve temporary egress rule for telemetry by 2026-10-08 (Priya)
SE to run 10k token throughput test and share raw CSV and summary by 2026-10-09 (Carlos)
Security docs (SOC2/ISO excerpt) to be uploaded to shared drive by Redwood (Lina)
action_items: Maya: raise support ticket for VPC peering/route-miss and ping infra by 2026-10-07
Priya: confirm egress exception for telemetry namespace by 2026-10-08
Carlos: execute long-tail latency run (10k token, mixed batch sizes) and upload results by 2026-10-09
Sara: provide KMS rotation policy and allowed CAs by 2026-10-12
transcript:
Header:
- Date: 2026-10-06
- Time: 10:30 AM PT
- Duration: ~42 minutes
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Lina (Redwood CSM), Owen (Redwood Platform), Priya (BrightCore SRE), Ethan (BrightCore ML), Sara (BrightCore Security), Daniel (BrightCore Product)

Summary: quick check-in for access and early latency numbers, ensure no staging gating items, align on next steps and evidence artifacts.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for jumping on — short agenda: access status, latency brief, any security gaps, and next steps. can we start with a quick round of where staging access is?
[00:18] Priya (BrightCore): yeah thanks, um so we gave the service account creds on monday, we verified the NATs, but we're still seeing route errors when peering to redwood-staging-usw. it's a 403-ish route-miss, not sure if it's on our side or the other side.
[00:35] Maya (Redwood): ok good, thanks. Carlos, do we have the peering tickets or logs from our side?
[00:41] Carlos (Redwood): i pulled the initial logs — looks like BGP flaps, but those could be noise; there was also an MTU mismatch on one of the subnets. i'll attach the support id — ff-support-1137 in the doc. Maya will open the ticket formally.
[00:55] Priya: MTU, huh. we had a custom MTU for the telemetry lane, maybe that is it. we'll double-check.
[01:03] Owen (Redwood): quick note — if MTU is off you can see packet drops that manifest as intermittent route failures; also make sure the firewall policy hasn't set a weird MSS clamp.
[01:12] Priya: got it, we'll check MSS.
[01:16] Daniel (BrightCore): on access: we still need one more port opened for telemetry (TCP 9443) for the ingestion proxy, is that a blocker?
[01:24] Lina (Redwood): temporary exception is fine for the POC — we usually prefer to avoid wide-egress, but for onboarding we'll permit that under a scoped timebox. we'll record it in the ticket.
[01:33] Sara (BrightCore): from security side, we need to see a SOC2 excerpt and KMS integration notes before we allow the exception end-of-week.
[01:41] Maya (Redwood): we'll share the SOC2 extract after this call, Lina will upload to the shared drive.
[01:48] Carlos: and for KMS, we need one item clarified — BrightCore's KMS rotates certs nightly; we support external KMS but we need a static service principal certificate or a short-lived handshake flow. how are you currently rotating?
[02:02] Sara: we rotate keys but keep a service principal with a short-lived cert. we can add Redwood's SP as an allowed principal, but we need to align on rotation window and audit log access.
[02:12] Owen: Redwood can support an HSM-backed flow or a delegated signing flow; for the POC we recommend delegated ephemeral tokens to avoid provisioning keys into our control plane. that will also simplify SOC auditability.
[02:25] Sara: ephemeral sounds ok, but we need to see the flow diagram.
[02:29] Carlos: i'll draw the flow and include which audit fields are emitted, and add it to the ticket.

[02:40] Maya: switching to latency — Carlos, you ran the preliminary bench last night? can you summarize?
[02:46] Carlos: yes. quick caveat: the model we used was community-7B-quant v2 (that's what the team requested for cost parity). numbers are: median p99 token-latency 85 ms at batch size 1 for 512 tokens; cold-start p99 spikes up to 600 ms for first token on cold KV-state; throughput sustained at about 170 reqs/minute on a 8xA100 pool for mixed prompts. there were some outliers at 2–3% where latency hit 1.2s — looking like garbage collection pauses in our runtime and a caching warm-up effect.
[03:23] Ethan (BrightCore): 85 ms p99 sounds reasonable. do you have the breakdown token vs network vs model infer?
[03:29] Carlos: yep — roughly 60 ms model, 15 ms kv cache lookup amortized, ~10 ms network inside the same AZ. we'll send the CSV.
[03:37] Daniel: what's the exact test harness? synthetic or replay?
[03:41] Carlos: replay of 2k real prompts from the pilot set, mixed sequence lengths skewed to 256 tokens median. but we need to run a long-tail 10k token test because your product sometimes has docs retrieval that stretches context.
[03:52] Priya: that 10k run is a yes from infra, as long as it doesn't consume our committed burst GPUs forever.
[03:58] Maya: we can schedule it as a one-off with a pre-agreed window. Carlos, run that and capture cold vs warm KV caches.
[04:06] Carlos: will do, i'll run both quantized and fp16 variants to show the tradeoff.

[04:12] Ethan: any expected quality delta when moving to quantized v2 versus fp16?
[04:16] Carlos: minimal for generation tasks at the parameter sizes you're using; we did see minor token-level edit distance increases on rare tokens, but we'll include evals on your prompt set.
[04:26] Daniel: can you also include a recommendation for batching config for our burst patterns? we've got spikes in mornings with small requests.
[04:33] Owen: for bursty small requests, a small continuous batching window (20–40ms) with a max batch of 8 strikes a good balance; we can show expected cost delta in the spreadsheet.

[04:44] Priya: telemetry — we noticed redwood telemetry emitted a lot of labels; is that configurable? we only want PII-free, aggregated metrics.
[04:51] Lina: yes it's configurable. we can send a minimal telemetry profile for the POC (no identifiers, aggregated at minute granularity).
[04:58] Sara: also need to know retention window — for us, 30 days is max for pre-prod.
[05:03] Lina: default is 90 days, but we'll set POC to 30 days and note that in the ticket.

[05:09] Priya: quick question — do you support mounting our internal registry model artifacts or do you require us to upload to Redwood model registry?
[05:16] Carlos: for Private deployments we can mount an internal registry via secure nfs or pull via ephemeral token; for Hosted POC the model lives in Redwood's registry but we can do a pull-through cache to avoid full uploads.
[05:29] Ethan: pull-through cache sounds better. lower friction. how about encrypted at-rest?
[05:33] Owen: yes, all model blob storage is encrypted with customer-managed keys when requested. we'll show the S3 kms workflow.

[05:40] Daniel: ok, can we recap blockers?
[05:43] Priya: MTU/MSS check and open telemetry port (9443), plus we need to review SOC2 excerpt and KMS rotation flow.
[05:52] Sara: one more — do you have RBAC mapping? we need to ensure principle-of-least-privilege for our dev ops.
[05:58] Maya: Redwood supports RBAC and SAML SSO; we'll send the mapping matrix. Lina will follow up with a template for roles.
[06:06] Carlos: technical note on KV priming: initial cold cache can cause up to ~400–600 ms spikes for first token; priming the cache with synthetic prefixes reduces that to under 100 ms. for your chat flows we recommend a lightweight cache priming at session start.
[06:25] Ethan: is that something the platform can do automatically or do we need client changes?
[06:29] Carlos: either — we can auto-warm based on recent retrievals or you can add a small prefix call in the client. we'll propose both options in the doc.

[06:36] Daniel: any concerns with long-run token costs with the warmup?
[06:40] Maya: cost is marginal if you use short priming patterns; batching and prefix sharing across users helps. our Optimize team will provide a sample config that minimizes tokens while getting cache benefits.
[06:50] Lina: shared artifact note — i uploaded a short benchmark spreadsheet and flow diagram to the shared drive (link: drive.redwood.com/teams/brightcore-poc/benchmarks). please check, i'll add the SOC2 excerpt after the call.
[07:03] Priya: saw the spreadsheet. Carlos, can you annotate which rows are cold vs warm?
[07:07] Carlos: yes will annotate and add raw CSVs.

[07:12] Sara: regarding audit logs: we need to ensure that request traces include the correlation id from our side, is that supported?
[07:19] Owen: yes, we accept incoming x-correlation-id and mirror it into the trace logs; we can redact sensitive fields but keep correlation id for triage.
[07:26] Sara: perfect.

[07:30] Maya: next: timeline — are we still on track for pilot start window next week?
[07:34] Priya: infrastructure-wise, yes if we get the egress exception and the peering fix. security needs SOC2/flow doc but said likely yes pending review.
[07:42] Daniel: product is ready for a smoke test next thursday.
[07:46] Maya: ok, goal is smoke test Thursday, production-like run Friday, and longer 10k token run over the weekend.

[07:53] Ethan: small ask — can you include quant profiles and the expected cost delta per 1M tokens? that's important for our finance review.
[07:59] Lina: we'll include an expected cost table with quant vs fp16 vs bf16.

[08:05] Priya: also, will there be a brief playbook for rollback if traffic spikes or errors appear?
[08:10] Owen: yes, we have a fallback policy for model variants and a traffic-shaping knob; we'll share the runbook.

[08:15] Maya: ok let's close with explicit next steps and owners — Lina, can you upload SOC2 excerpt and RBAC template today?
[08:22] Lina: yes, will upload within 2 hours.
[08:25] Maya: Carlos, run the 10k token cold/warm runs and share results by Friday.
[08:29] Carlos: confirmed.
[08:31] Priya: i'll confirm egress exception by Friday morning.
[08:34] Sara: i'll send KMS rotation policy by Monday.

[08:38] Maya: awesome. any final questions?
[08:41] Daniel: none from product. thanks everyone.
[08:44] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up with the ticket id and deck.

End of call.
